payment_channel.title: Payment through a personal or untraceable channel
payment_channel.detail: Universities and licensed employers take fees into an account in their own name, not JazzCash, Easypaisa, money transfer services or crypto.

payee_mismatch.title: Money goes to someone other than the issuer
payee_mismatch.detail: The document is from “{issuer}” but asks you to pay someone else.

free_email.title: Uses a free email address
free_email.detail: Real universities, embassies and employers write from their own domain, not from Gmail or other free email.

email_domain_mismatch.title: Email domain differs from the website
email_domain_mismatch.detail: The website is {site} but emails come from {domains}. Look-alike domains are a common trick.

ref_format.title: {kind, select, cas {CAS number} dli {DLI number} cricos {CRICOS code} sevis {SEVIS ID} other {Reference number}} has the wrong format
ref_format.detail: {kind, select, cas {A UK CAS number has 14 letters and digits.} dli {A Canadian DLI number is the letter O followed by 11 to 13 digits.} cricos {A CRICOS provider code is 5 digits and a letter.} sevis {A US SEVIS ID is N followed by 10 digits.} other {The number doesn’t match the official format.}}

pressure.title: Pressure to act fast
pressure.detail: The document pushes you to pay or decide within days, threatens you, or asks you to keep it secret. Real institutions give you time to check.

embedded_instructions.title: Hidden instructions aimed at checking tools
embedded_instructions.detail: The document contains text that tries to instruct an AI or a reviewer. A genuine letter has no reason to do this.

job_fee.title: Job offer asks for money
job_fee.detail: Fees for visas, tickets or “processing” before you start are the most common overseas job scam. Licensed promoters may only charge the fee set by the Bureau of Emigration, against a receipt.

internship_fee.title: Internship asks for money
internship_fee.detail: Real internships do not charge registration, training or security fees. Asking interns to pay up front is a common scam, including fake ads in the name of government bodies.

pdf_editor.title: PDF was made or edited with a consumer editing tool
pdf_editor.detail: The file says it was produced by “{tool}”. Official letters are usually generated by the institution’s own system.

pdf_modified.title: PDF was changed after it was created
pdf_modified.detail: Created {created}, modified {modified}. Not proof of fraud, but worth confirming with the issuer.

domain_new.title: Website or email domain is very new
domain_new.detail: {domain} was registered on {date}, {days} days ago. Established institutions have had their domain for years.

domain_age_unavailable.title: Domain age could not be verified
domain_age_unavailable.detail: RDAP returned no registration date for {domain}, so its age could not be checked.

ukvi_listed.title: Listed on the UK student sponsor register
ukvi_listed.detail: UKVI lists “{listed}”. This confirms the institution exists and can sponsor students. It does not confirm this letter is real.

ukvi_not_found.title: Not found on the UK student sponsor register under this name
ukvi_not_found.detail: No sponsor named “{issuer}” is on today’s UKVI register. Only listed sponsors can issue a CAS for a UK student visa. Search the register yourself in case the letter uses a short or different name.

register_code_missing.title: {register, select, dli {DLI number} cricos {CRICOS code} other {Register number}} {code} is not on the register
register_code_missing.detail: {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {The register}} has no institution with this number. Scammers often invent or alter these numbers.

register_code_other.title: {register, select, dli {DLI number} cricos {CRICOS code} other {Register number}} {code} belongs to a different institution
register_code_other.detail: {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {The register}} lists {code} as “{listed}”, not “{issuer}”. Scammers copy real numbers from other institutions.

register_code_match.title: {register, select, dli {DLI number} cricos {CRICOS code} other {Register number}} {code} matches {listed}
register_code_match.detail: {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {The register}} lists this number for “{listed}”. This confirms the institution exists, not that this letter is real.

register_listed.title: Listed on {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {the register}}
register_listed.detail: It lists “{listed}”. This confirms the institution exists and can enrol international students. It does not confirm this letter is real.

register_not_found.title: Not found on {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {the register}} under this name
register_not_found.detail: No institution named “{issuer}” is on it. Search it yourself in case the letter uses a short or different name.

register_website_differs.title: Website or email differs from the registered website
register_website_differs.detail: {register, select, dli {Canada’s designated learning institutions list} cricos {Australia’s CRICOS register} other {The register}} gives {official} as the website of “{listed}”, but the document uses {domains}.

pkcert_match.title: Matches a notice National CERT (PKCERT) has declared fake
pkcert_match.detail: PKCERT recorded a fake notice “{notice}”{date, select, none {} other { on {date}}}. {match, select, shared {It shares {shared} with this document.} other {This document has the same subject.}} Compare the two before acting on it.

lookalike_domain.title: Domain looks like the official one but is different
lookalike_domain.detail: {kind, select, tld {The document uses {domain}: the same name as the official domain {official}, with a different ending.} embedded {The document uses {domain}, which contains the name of the official domain {official} but is a different domain.} other {The document uses {domain}, one or two letters away from the official domain {official}.}} Scammers register look-alike domains to seem official. Use only {official}.

check_failed.title: {check, select, rules {Rule checks} pdf {The PDF metadata check} domain_age {The domain age check} ukvi {The UK sponsor register check} dli {The Canadian DLI list check} cricos {The Australian CRICOS register check} pkcert {The PKCERT fake notification check} web_research {Web research} summary {The written report} other {A check}} could not run
check_failed.detail: This could not be verified, so the result can’t be “no red flags found”. Try again later.

source_unavailable.title: {check, select, rules {Rule checks} pdf {The PDF metadata check} domain_age {The domain age check} ukvi {The UK sponsor register check} dli {The Canadian DLI list check} cricos {The Australian CRICOS register check} pkcert {The PKCERT fake notification check} web_research {Web research} summary {The written report} other {A check}} could not run
source_unavailable.detail: This source could not be reached, so this could not be verified. It does not change the risk level.

reports.intro: Reports you chose to save from the document checker. Each one shows what was found when you ran the check.

reports.deleteFailed: The report could not be deleted. Try again.
